newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro stocks mixed, unsettled by US jobs data.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro stocks mixed, unsettled by US jobs data.

text.p: European bourses were mixed on Friday, unsettled ahead of the release U.S. jobless figures that will throw light on inflation pressures and interest rate prospects in the world's largest economy.
The dollar was virtually unchanged from Thursday's European closing levels as forex traders weighed the chances of higher interest rates if the data, due at 1230 GMT, showed strong employment growth.

London stocks, which scaled new peaks only two days ago, fell in slow trading as the jitters took hold. Paris, too, shed some of its recent gains but Frankfurt managed to edge ahead to touch a new trading peak though volumes were thin.
German stocks slipped in thin trading but recovered by midday to touch a new high of 2683.14 on the DAX index eclipsing the previous intra-day high set two days ago.
The bourse's performance was helped by the dollar's recent strength against the mark, which boosts export prospects, but trading was thin after Thursday's Unity Day holiday.

"Most people closed their books for the week on Wednesday ahead of the holiday." said one trader. Trading on Frankfurt's computerised IBIS index was down. London's FTSE 100 index slipped 0.3 percent, getting little direction from Wall Street, which ended on negative ground at 5,932.85 after gaining 65 points in the past four sessions.
"There's no enthusiasm to take the market higher until we see those numbers," said one broker. "The phones aren't ringing. Clients are holding back."

"There's not going to be a huge amount of tolerance for very strong numbers because of how far we've gone up," said one dealer. "From where we stand at the moment, there's more of a risk of an adverse reaction."
The closely-watched statistics on U.S. non-farm payrolls for September will provide a fresh picture of the power-house American economy.

A big increase in jobs could suggest inflationary pressures may prompt the Federal Reserve central bank to tighten credit, bad news for business. Conversely, poor U.S. employment figures could boost European equities.
Economists surveyed by Reuters expect an increase of 166,000 non-agricultural jobs in September after an upturn of 250,000 in August.
French shares sagged 0.2 percent and dealers said the market was drifting ahead of the U.S. unemployment data.
The upcoming American figures also dominated the foreign exchanges which were quiet, with the dollar barely moving, and dealers reported no enthusiasm to break out of current levels.

"The market would prefer to buy dollars. That's the attitude at the moment, but we still need some good figures today to determine the follow-through," said Alan Collins, head of technical analysis at Merita Bank.

But there was some ambiguity in market views. Strong data will add weight to the argument for higher near-term U.S. rates, which usually helps the dollar, but the likely gloom in the U.S. bond and stock markets could have the opposite effect.
"The converse would be likely in case of a soft figure, which would undermine the interest rate support the dollar enjoys," said Klaus Baader, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell economist.
CURRENCIES AT 1115 GMT
The dollar traded around 111.56 yen and 1.5307 marks versus Thursday's late European levels of 111.47 and 1.5291.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1115 GMT
London - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading shares was down 15.6 points at 3,984.4.
Paris - The CAC-40 share index was down 4.62 points at 2,131.47.
Frankfurt - The 30-share DAX index was up 4.41 points at 2680.91.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $380.20 an ounce in the morning, versus Thursday's close of $379.35. Silver was unchanged at $4.91.
